messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Problem with truncation
parts:
So I just realized today that Stan is missing one major piece for
distribution truncation to work properly. A parameter outside the
truncation range is not given zero probability. That is if we have

x ~ normal(mu,sigma) T[-1,1];

and x takes on a value outside of [-1,1] (for whatever reason) lp__
should be incremented by -infinity. In most properly specified
models, this should never come up because either x is data and lies in
the range or x is a parameter with a matching bounded definition so
never takes on a value outside the range.

However, poorly written models where x is properly bound could give
incorrect answers rather than just sample very slowly. Further, a
model where the parameters of the truncation are themselves parameters
will never work with the current code. The fix should be
straightforward, just add a call to a function which checks the bounds
and either adds nothing to lp__ or adds -infinity to lp__ if a sample
is outside the bounds.

Unfortunately, I don't have time to do this right now but hopefully
someone else will.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Problem with truncation
parts:
On 9/26/12 12:16 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> ... A parameter outside the

> truncation range is not given zero probability. That is if we have
>
> x ~ normal(mu,sigma) T[-1,1];
>
> and x takes on a value outside of [-1,1] (for whatever reason) lp__
> should be incremented by -infinity.

Absolutely.

I'll fix it. Returning -inf matches the decision to return -inf for log
prob of variates outside the support of the distribution.

We should also add vectorization. As is, vectorized code with
truncations shouldn't compile because there's no matching cdf.

- Bob
